item.title: JVM Architecture
item.description:
The JVM Specification defines an abstract execution model, not an operating system memory map. An implementation may use JIT compilation, moving garbage collection, contiguous or segmented storage, and native metadata while preserving the specified behavior.

Runtime Data Areas #

Each JVM thread has a program-counter register, a JVM stack, and optionally a native-method stack. The PC identifies the current JVM instruction for Java code and has an undefined value while native code executes. A JVM stack holds frames; failure to create a frame produces StackOverflowError for a size limit or OutOfMemoryError when an expandable stack cannot grow.

item.title: C++ Implementation Idioms
item.description:
An implementation idiom should make an ownership, lifetime, or dependency boundary explicit. Concise syntax is useful only when the associated invalidation and complexity rules remain visible to the reader.

Erase-Remove for Sequence Containers #

std::remove and std::remove_if are algorithms; they rearrange a range so retained elements occupy a prefix and return the new logical end. They neither erase elements nor change a container’s size. Erase the suffix immediately when the container provides an erase range overload.

item.title: Linux Kernel Locking
item.description:
Kernel locking begins with execution context. A lock that is correct between process-context callers can deadlock when the same data is reached from a softirq, hard interrupt, or nonmaskable interrupt (NMI). The primitive and its suffix must match every context that accesses the protected state.

Spin-Lock Semantics #

Declare and initialize ordinary spin locks with:

c 
static DEFINE_SPINLOCK(queue_lock);

struct queue {
 spinlock_t lock;
};

spin_lock_init(&queue->lock);

On a non-PREEMPT_RT SMP kernel, spin_lock() disables preemption on the local CPU and spins until it acquires exclusive ownership. It does not disable local interrupts or softirqs. A holder must not sleep, schedule explicitly, perform a blocking allocation, or call code that can acquire a sleeping lock.

item.title: JVM Classfile Format
item.description:
A class file is a big-endian binary structure consumed by the JVM. It begins with 0xCAFEBABE, followed by u2 minor and major versions. A JVM accepts only the versions defined for its implementation; class-file parsers must reject unsupported versions rather than assume that a newer file is backward-compatible.

Top-Level Structure #

After the magic and version, the file contains:

  1. constant_pool_count and the indexed constant-pool entries;
  2. class access_flags, this_class, and super_class;
  3. interface indexes;
  4. field_info structures;
  5. method_info structures; and
  6. class-level attribute_info structures.

Counts are unsigned u2 values, except an attribute’s attribute_length, which is u4. Access flags describe the context: ACC_PUBLIC, ACC_FINAL, ACC_SUPER, ACC_INTERFACE, ACC_ABSTRACT, ACC_SYNTHETIC, ACC_ANNOTATION, ACC_ENUM, and ACC_MODULE are not all meaningful or legal for every class-file kind.

item.title: 19-Inch Server Racks
item.description:
A 19-inch rack standardizes the front-panel and mounting geometry for telecommunications, computing, network, and audio equipment. The nominal 19-inch dimension describes the panel width across the mounting ears; it does not specify cabinet width, rail spacing, equipment depth, power, or cooling.

Rack Units, Hole Patterns, and Rails #

One rack unit (U or RU) is 1.75 inches (44.45 mm). A 1U interval contains three vertically spaced mounting holes. The center-to-center pattern is 0.625 inch, 0.625 inch, and 0.5 inch before it repeats, so adjacent rack-unit boundaries can be identified by the narrower gap. Number rails consistently because mounting a chassis across a boundary offsets every later installation.

item.title: C++ Copy Elision and Return Values
item.description:
Copy elision permits an implementation to omit copy or move construction even when that constructor or destructor has observable side effects. Before C++17, every elision case was permitted but optional. C++17 changed prvalue semantics, making several former temporary-elision cases direct construction instead.

Returned Prvalues and Named Locals #

item.title: C++ Random Number Facilities
item.description:
The C++ random library separates a deterministic engine from a distribution. An engine produces a sequence of uniformly distributed values over its specified output range. A distribution consumes engine output and maps it to a requested statistical distribution. Keep both objects alive when their state must continue.

cpp 
#include <random>

std::mt19937_64 engine{std::random_device{}()};
std::uniform_int_distribution<int> die{1, 6};

int roll = die(engine); // Both engine and distribution may advance state.

std::mt19937 and std::mt19937_64 are pseudo-random engines: a fixed initial state produces a reproducible sequence. std::default_random_engine is implementation-defined, so it is unsuitable when tests, files, or protocols require the same sequence across implementations.

item.title: Linux Randomness APIs
item.description:
Randomness APIs serve two different contracts. Deterministic pseudo-random number generators are useful for repeatable tests and simulations. Security-sensitive keys, nonces, tokens, salts, and seeds require bytes from the kernel’s cryptographically secure random number generator (CSPRNG).

C Library Generators #

rand() advances hidden process state and returns an integer from 0 through RAND_MAX. srand(seed) selects a repeatable sequence for a particular C library implementation; omitting it behaves as though the seed were 1. ISO C does not specify the algorithm or require the same sequence across implementations, so a test that needs cross-platform reproducibility should choose and record an explicit algorithm.

item.title: Linux Kernel Virtualization
item.description:
KVM exposes Linux hardware virtualization through /dev/kvm. KVM supplies the kernel execution mechanism, while a virtual machine monitor such as QEMU constructs and operates a complete guest machine.

Division of Responsibilities #

KVM uses Intel VT-x, AMD-V, Arm virtualization extensions, or the corresponding host facility to execute guest instructions directly when possible. Kernel code manages vCPU state, second-stage memory translation, interrupt delivery, timers, and transitions between guest and host execution. KVM intentionally does not provide a complete firmware and device model.

item.title: Java Service Provider Interface
item.description:
Java SPI separates a service contract from one or more providers and from the consumer that selects them. The consumer depends on the service type and uses ServiceLoader, so providers can be added at deployment without an application dependency on concrete classes.

Classpath Services #

Before modules, a provider JAR listed implementations in META-INF/services/<fully.qualified.ServiceName>. The UTF-8 file has one provider class name per line; blank lines and # comments are allowed. Each provider must be accessible to the loader used for discovery and offer a public no-argument constructor.

item.title: MySQL String Types and Character Sets
item.description:
MySQL string columns have both a logical character limit and a physical byte representation. Keeping those ideas separate prevents many surprises with multilingual text and indexes.

CHAR and VARCHAR #

CHAR(n) is a fixed-length character string. MySQL pads values to its declared length for storage semantics, so it is best for genuinely fixed-width values such as country codes. VARCHAR(n) is variable length and is usually the better default for names, labels, and other text whose length varies.

item.title: Web Fonts and Browser Font Selection

A typeface, or font family, groups related faces. A face has properties such as weight, style, and stretch. A glyph is the rendered shape selected for a character or character sequence.

Browser font selection happens per character. A paragraph can therefore use one family for Latin letters, another for CJK characters, and an emoji font for emoji.

item.title: C++ Classes and Special Member Functions
item.description:
A C++ class defines representation, invariants, and the operations that establish and preserve them. Constructors establish an object’s invariant, member functions preserve it, and the destructor releases resources owned by that object. Design the ownership policy first, because it determines whether compiler-generated special members are correct.

Construction and Destruction #

A constructor has the class name and no return type. A default constructor has no parameters or has defaults for all its parameters. Copy and move constructors initialize a new object from an lvalue or rvalue of the same class; copy and move assignment update an existing object.

item.title: Sizing HTML Canvas Elements
item.description:
An HTML canvas has two sizes:

  1. The width and height attributes define its drawing buffer.
  2. CSS width and height define its displayed box.

Confusing the two sizes produces blurred output, stretched coordinates, or excessive memory use.

Drawing Buffer and Display Size #

Canvas attributes contain unitless pixel counts:

html 
<canvas width="800" height="400"></canvas>

The default drawing buffer is 300 by 150 pixels. CSS can display that buffer at another size:

css 
canvas {
 inline-size: 100%;
 block-size: auto;
}

When the CSS box and drawing buffer have different aspect ratios, the browser stretches the bitmap. Writing width="800px" is invalid in intent because the attribute is an integer, not a CSS length.

item.title: LZ77 Sliding-Window Compression
item.description:
LZ77 is a family of lossless compressors that replaces repeated input with references into a bounded history window. The original 1977 design used a sliding dictionary; practical formats choose their own token syntax, match finder, and entropy coder.

Literals, History, and Matches #

At an input position, the encoder searches the previously emitted bytes for a matching prefix. It emits a literal when no useful match exists, or a back-reference containing at least a distance and a length. Some formats add a literal after every match; others emit a stream of independent literals and matches. The decoder copies length bytes from distance bytes before its current output position.

item.title: x86 Architectural Registers
item.description:
x86 architectural registers hold programmer-visible integer, control, status, address-translation, debug, floating-point, and vector state. Width and availability depend on execution mode and enabled extensions. Calling conventions assign software roles to a subset of these registers but do not change their architectural behavior.

General-Purpose Registers and Subregisters #

IA-32 exposes EAX, EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI, EDI, EBP, and ESP. x86-64 widens them to RAX through RSP and adds R8 through R15. Subregisters name parts of the same architectural register:

item.title: HTTP Video Streaming
item.description: HTTP video delivery ranges from one seekable file to an adaptive sequence of short media segments. HTTP moves representations and validators; a container organizes timed tracks, and codecs encode the audio and video samples. Keeping those layers separate makes range handling, caching, and playback failures easier to diagnose.

item.title: Coding Theory
item.description: Coding theory describes how symbols are represented, transmitted, and recovered. In a software system, “coding” can mean compression, an error code, a wire-level signal, or a framing convention. Those mechanisms interact, but they solve different problems.

item.title: Computer Graphics Rendering Basics
item.description: Rendering turns abstract geometry into pixels. A GPU pipeline takes vertices, transforms them, clips them, rasterizes the visible shapes, and shades the resulting fragments.

item.title: Disk Addressing and Partition Tables
item.description: Disk addresses identify sectors, while partition tables divide the resulting address space into regions. Filesystems occupy some of those regions but belong to a separate format layer. Keeping the layers distinct explains why obsolete geometry fields can coexist with modern logical addressing.

item.title: FAT Filesystems
item.description: The File Allocation Table (FAT) family began on small Microsoft systems and became the interchange format for DOS and IBM PC media. Simple data structures made FAT practical in boot firmware and constrained operating systems. The same design omits journaling, ownership, and transaction semantics, so interoperability rather than failure isolation explains its continued use.

item.title: GObject and GTK Type System
item.description: GTK builds its object model on GType and GObject. GType records runtime type relationships and metadata; GObject adds reference-counted instances, properties, and signals; GIO and GTK then use those facilities for actions and widgets. C macros generate repetitive registration code, but the object and class layouts remain ordinary C structures.

item.title: Hugo Site Build Lifecycle
item.description: Hugo builds a site from configuration, mounted files, content metadata, templates, and resources. File placement is part of the data model because it determines page kind, bundle boundaries, and template lookup.

item.title: Hugo Templates and Shortcodes
item.description: Hugo templates combine Go’s template language with Hugo functions and page objects. Shortcodes use the same language, but content authors invoke them from Markdown while Hugo constructs .Content.

item.title: IDE ATA Storage
item.description: Integrated Drive Electronics moved disk-specific control logic onto the drive and standardized the host-facing registers and commands. The resulting ATA family dominated PC storage before Serial ATA, but several related names describe different parts of that history.

item.title: JavaScript Script Loading
item.description: The HTML parser, script fetcher, and JavaScript engine can work concurrently, but execution constraints differ by script type and attributes. Choose a mode from the dependency graph and readiness contract rather than adding async or defer only as a performance hint.

item.title: Optical Media and Disc Images
item.description: Optical media, sector formats, filesystems, and image files are separate layers. A mountable .iso can reproduce a data volume while omitting audio tracks, session boundaries, subchannels, and recording properties. Image format must therefore follow the intended task: file distribution, booting, emulation, or preservation.

item.title: Sudo Source Code Guide
item.description: The sudo source tree separates front-end programs, plugin implementations, reusable libraries, generated language parsers, and portability support. Start from an executable’s entry point, then follow the plugin interface; reading the tree by directory name alone obscures the policy boundary.

item.title: TypeScript Enums and Value Types
item.description: A closed set can require a compile-time constraint, a runtime lookup object, a wire representation, or a domain object with validated behavior. TypeScript offers different representations because those requirements are not equivalent.

item.title: ELF Format
item.description:
ELF is the object and executable format used by Linux and many Unix-like systems. Its ELF header locates the program-header table, used by the loader, and the section-header table, used mainly by linkers and other tooling.

Sections #

Sections organize object-file content such as code, data, symbols, relocations, and string tables. They are not the same as loadable segments: a linker groups sections into segments according to the runtime memory layout.

item.title: Linux System Calls
item.description:
Linux system calls form an architecture-specific binary interface between a process and the kernel. Application code normally targets a C library API instead, because the library supplies types, feature-test macros, compatibility behavior, and the machine-specific entry sequence.

Library API and Kernel ABI #

A source-level call such as open(path, flags) is not a promise to execute a kernel system call named open. glibc can implement it with openat, add cancellation checks, or select a time-width-compatible entry point. Functions such as clock_gettime can execute in the vDSO without entering the kernel. Conversely, Linux exposes system calls such as gettid for which older C libraries did not provide a wrapper.

item.title: GLib Main Loop
item.description: GLib’s event loop separates event descriptions from event dispatch. A GSource describes when work is ready, a GMainContext owns and schedules a set of sources, and a GMainLoop repeatedly iterates one context. Keeping those roles separate makes callback placement, cancellation, and lifetime rules explicit.

item.title: x86 Memory Organization
item.description:
x86 memory organization developed in response to successive limits on register width, address-bus width, protection, and multitasking. Physical memory remains a byte-addressed space: after translation, the processor places a physical address on the memory interface. The path to that address, however, has changed substantially.

An x86 instruction first computes an effective address (EA), also called an offset. In modes with usable segmentation, a selected segment contributes a base, producing a linear address. With paging enabled, page tables translate the linear address to a physical address. The stages are therefore:

item.description:
JAX-RS is the Jakarta standard API and specification for HTTP resources in the jakarta.ws.rs packages. It defines annotations, request and response types, client APIs, providers, and server-sent event support. Jersey is a conforming JAX-RS implementation.

JAX-RS is distinct from JAX-WS, which concerns XML web services.

Add the Jakarta REST API at compile time and a JAX-RS implementation at runtime. A resource class uses @Path; methods use an HTTP method annotation and may add a relative path:

item.title: Huffman Coding
item.description:
Huffman coding maps symbols to variable-length bit strings. A prefix-free code has no codeword that is a prefix of another, so a decoder can walk one binary tree and emit a symbol as soon as it reaches a leaf. Prefix-free codes are uniquely decodable, although uniquely decodable codes do not all have the prefix-free property.

item.title: DEC Modules and the PDP-7
item.description:
Digital Equipment Corporation (DEC) built its first computers from cataloged logic modules rather than custom monolithic processor boards. Module packaging changed substantially between the laboratory products, System Modules, and FLIP CHIP cards, but the engineering method remained recognizable: combine standardized gates, flip-flops, pulse circuits, and drivers through a wired backplane.

Laboratory Modules #

DEC introduced Laboratory Modules in the late 1950s for digital experiments and control systems. A metal enclosure held a transistorized circuit with banana-plug connections on the front. Engineers could patch modules together on a bench or install them in a rack chassis. Catalogs offered functional blocks such as inverters, flip-flops, pulse amplifiers, delays, clocks, and power supplies in families intended for different switching rates.

item.title: Java Enums and Interfaces
item.description:
An enum declaration defines a final class with a fixed set of instances. Each constant is an instance of that class, which conceptually extends Enum<E> with the enum type as E; no user enum may extend another class. The compiler supplies values() and valueOf(String), while Enum supplies the name, ordinal, comparison, and serialization rules.

Interfaces and Constant-Specific Behavior #

An enum may implement interfaces, and the implementation can be shared by all constants or supplied in a constant-specific class body.

item.title: Regular Expressions
item.description: Regular expressions are not one language. POSIX BRE, POSIX ERE, and Perl-compatible engines overlap, but they differ in syntax, matching rules, and available features.

item.title: C++ Exceptions and Exception Safety
item.description:
Exceptions separate reporting a failed operation from propagating it to a boundary that can respond. An exception transfers control to a matching handler; while control travels outward, C++ destroys every fully constructed automatic object whose scope is exited, in reverse construction order. Resource acquisition is initialization (RAII) therefore makes the normal and exceptional cleanup paths the same.

cpp 
void load_configuration(std::filesystem::path path) {
 std::ifstream input{path}; // Closed during unwinding.
 if (!input) {
 throw std::runtime_error{"cannot open configuration"};
 }
 // Parsing may throw; input still closes.
}

try {
 load_configuration("app.conf");
} catch (const std::exception& error) {
 report(error.what());
}

Throw exception objects by value and catch polymorphic exception types by const reference. Catching a base exception by value slices a derived object. A catch (...) belongs only at a boundary that can restore an invariant, translate an error, or deliberately terminate; it must not silently continue with damaged state.

item.title: Web Icons
item.description: Web icons can be text glyphs, SVG graphics, or bitmap images. Format selection affects rendering fidelity, caching, styling, security, and the accessible name exposed by the surrounding control.

item.title: awk
item.description:
awk transforms text as a stream of records. Each record is tested against ordered pattern-action rules, which makes the language suited to reports, validation, and small data transformations. POSIX awk is widely available; GNU awk (gawk) adds features that scripts should declare when they require them.

Records, Fields, and Counters #

RS separates input records and defaults to newline. FS separates fields; its default treats runs of spaces and tabs specially. $0 is the whole record, $1 through $NF are fields, and NF is the field count. NR counts records across all inputs, whereas FNR restarts for each input file.

item.title: GNU Autotools
item.description:
GNU Autotools generates portable build interfaces from project metadata. Autoconf probes the build environment and emits configure; Automake generates portable Makefile.in templates from Makefile.am; Libtool abstracts platform-specific library linking. The generated files are designed for source releases, whereas maintainers edit the .ac, .am, and m4 inputs.

item.title: Formal Logic and Computation
item.description: Formal logic separates the shape of an argument from the subject it discusses. Syntax defines admissible expressions and proofs; semantics assigns interpretations and truth conditions. Relating the two makes it possible to state precisely what a proof system can establish and what a computational model can decide.

item.title: Electronics Fundamentals
item.description:
Circuit analysis models how electric fields move charge and store or dissipate energy. Voltage is electric potential difference, current is charge flow per unit time, and power is the rate of energy transfer:

text 
V = I R
P = V I

Ohm’s law applies to a linear resistance, not to every component. Practical designs must also satisfy voltage, current, power, temperature, frequency, and transient ratings.

Resistance, Capacitance, and Inductance #

A resistor dissipates electrical energy as heat. Resistance is measured in ohms, while conductance is its reciprocal and is measured in siemens. Resistivity is a material property; a part’s resistance also depends on its geometry and temperature.

item.title: systemd
item.description:
systemd is a service manager and a suite of Linux system-management components. The system manager runs as PID 1; per-user managers run as systemd --user. Both managers load units, calculate transactions of jobs, and supervise process groups through Linux control groups.

Units, Jobs, and Lifecycle States #

A unit represents a resource known to a manager. Common unit types are:

Suffix Resource
.service A process or daemon
.socket An IPC or network socket used for activation
.target A synchronization and grouping point
.mount, .automount, .swap Storage configuration
.device, .path, .timer Device or event-based activation
.slice, .scope cgroup organization and externally started processes

A job is a requested unit state change such as start, stop, or reload. Starting one unit can pull in other jobs; the manager combines them into a transaction, checks for ordering cycles and conflicting jobs, and then dispatches independent work in parallel.

item.title: Curl
item.description: curl transfers a URL with an ordered command line: options configure one or more transfers, and every URL starts a transfer. It supports many protocols; examples below use HTTP because its request and response controls are common.

item.title: zlib Streaming API
item.description:
zlib is a C library that implements DEFLATE and its common wrappers. Its streaming API uses z_stream, so an application can process input and output in bounded buffers instead of assuming that one call consumes or produces a whole message.

Stream State and Initialization #

The application supplies next_in/avail_in and next_out/avail_out. After a call, zlib advances the pointers and decreases the available counts; total_in and total_out provide cumulative counters. The application must consume produced bytes and refill buffers before the next call, while leaving the other state fields to zlib.

item.title: Man Pages
item.description:
Manual pages are reference documents installed with software. Section numbers distinguish subjects: section 1 documents user commands, 2 system calls, 3 library functions, 4 device and special files, 5 file formats and conventions, 7 overviews and protocols, and 8 administrative commands. A qualified lookup selects the intended page:

sh 
man 2 open
man 3 printf
man 5 passwd

Sections, Names, and Synopses #

Select a page by both name and section because the same name can describe a command, function, or file. Page source and installed filenames conventionally use name.section, such as printf.1 and printf.3. The NAME section provides name \- one-line description; tools such as apropos index that line. The SYNOPSIS follows command-line notation for commands and declaration notation for APIs.

item.title: Linux Printing
item.description:
CUPS provides an Internet Printing Protocol (IPP) client and scheduler. A CUPS destination is a named printer queue or class; a physical or network printer is the device reached by that queue. Consequently, queue state, job state, and device reachability are separate diagnostic concerns.

Queues, Printers, and IPP #

Clients encode job documents and attributes in IPP requests. A local client commonly connects to the scheduler over a Unix-domain socket, while a remote client uses ipp:// or encrypted ipps://, conventionally on TCP port 631. The scheduler spools the job, selects a destination, converts data when required, and sends output through a backend or a driverless IPP connection.

item.title: Git Internals and History Editing
item.description:
Git stores immutable objects and moves small references between them. Daily work should use porcelain commands, while the storage model explains why rewrites create new history and why recovery remains possible for a period.

Inspect the Repository Database #

The .git directory contains repository-local state:

Path Purpose
HEAD Symbolic name of the checked-out branch, or a detached object ID
config Repository configuration
index Proposed snapshot for the next commit
objects/ Loose objects and packfiles
refs/ and packed-refs Branch, tag, and remote-tracking names
logs/ Local reflogs for references
hooks/ Client-side hook samples and installed hooks
modules/ Git directories for initialized submodules

A worktree holds checked-out files. The index records a candidate tree. A commit points to a tree together with parent IDs and metadata. A branch is a movable reference to a commit; it is not a mutable container of commits.

item.title: C++ Smart Pointers and Ownership
item.description:
Smart pointers make ownership visible in an interface. They do not replace references and raw pointers used solely to borrow an object whose lifetime is guaranteed elsewhere. Select the pointer type from the lifetime contract, then make transfer and observation explicit at API boundaries.

Unique Ownership #

std::unique_ptr<T> owns one object and is move-only. Create it with std::make_unique when ordinary new and the default deleter are appropriate; pass or return it by value to transfer ownership.

Quay is a container-image registry product from Red Hat. It stores and distributes OCI and Docker-compatible images, with organization and repository access controls, robot accounts, vulnerability scanning integrations, and optional repository mirroring. A registry is not a source-control system: image tags identify published artifacts, while source and build definitions should remain in version control.

item.title: Cryptographic Hash Functions
item.description: Cryptographic hash functions reduce arbitrary byte strings to fixed-size digests. Protocols rely on specific resistance properties rather than on the mere act of hashing, because a fast unkeyed digest provides neither message authentication nor safe password storage.

item.title: FFmpeg User Guide
item.description: ffmpeg is a media pipeline tool. It reads one or more inputs, optionally filters the decoded frames, and writes one or more outputs.

item.title: Spring Resources
item.description:
org.springframework.core.io.Resource gives Spring APIs one handle for content that may reside in a file, classpath entry, URL, servlet context, byte array, or already-open stream. The abstraction describes access capabilities; it does not make every resource seekable, repeatable, writable, or backed by a file.

The Resource Contract #

Resource extends InputStreamSource. getInputStream() is the fundamental operation, while methods such as exists(), isReadable(), isOpen(), isFile(), contentLength(), lastModified(), and getDescription() expose capabilities or metadata.

item.title: Early x86 Processor Models
item.description:
Processor models share an ISA lineage but differ in buses, packages, clocks, integrated peripherals, and microarchitecture. Software compatibility therefore does not imply identical board-level behavior.

Intel 8086 and 8088 #

The 8086 and 8088 execute the same 16-bit instruction set and use a 20-bit address space, providing 1 MiB of physical memory. Their principal external difference is the data bus: the 8086 has a 16-bit bus, while the 8088 has an 8-bit bus. The reduced bus width made the 8088 easier to connect to contemporary low-cost peripherals, at the cost of additional bus cycles for 16-bit transfers.

item.title: Scala Starter Pack
item.description:
Scala compiles to JVM bytecode. A build requires a Scala compiler at compile time and the Scala standard library on the application runtime classpath. Scala binary versions are compatibility boundaries: an artifact ending in _2.13 is not interchangeable with its _3 counterpart.

Versions and Toolchains #

Scala 2 and Scala 3 have distinct compilers and language rules. Use the binary version selected by the project for every cross-published library. The Java runtime must meet the Scala release’s documented JDK requirements; compile and test with the JDK used in deployment.

item.title: Redis Data Types and Commands
item.description:
Redis associates each key with one data type. A command issued against a key of the wrong type fails, so key naming and value ownership should make the data model explicit.

Redis executes each command atomically on the server thread. Single commands such as INCR, HSET, SADD, and ZADD are therefore safe for one-key state changes, but multi-step read-modify-write sequences need MULTI/EXEC, WATCH, or Lua if they must behave as one unit.

item.title: CSS Properties and Standards
item.description: CSS is organized as a standards family, not as a single versioned language. The specification evolves in levels and modules, while browsers implement a moving subset of those documents.

item.title: C++ Static Initialization Order
item.description:
C++ assigns storage duration independently of scope. Initialization and destruction rules for static and thread storage determine whether an object is available before main, on first use, or once per thread.

Storage Duration and Initialization Phases #

Namespace-scope objects, static data members, and block-scope static objects have static storage duration. thread_local objects have thread storage duration: each thread has a distinct instance, initialized as that thread starts or first uses it according to the declaration and implementation rules.

item.title: CUDA Fundamentals
item.description:
CUDA is NVIDIA’s platform for general-purpose GPU computing. CUDA C++ extends C++ with constructs for launching work on a GPU, while the nvcc compiler coordinates host compilation and device-code compilation. It is not a separate replacement for C++; it is a programming model and toolchain built around NVIDIA GPUs.

The Execution Model #

A CPU program, called host code, launches a kernel on the GPU. The kernel runs many lightweight threads. Threads are grouped into blocks, and blocks form a grid. Threads within a block can cooperate through fast shared memory and synchronization; blocks are designed to run independently so the GPU can schedule them across multiprocessors.

item.title: Spring Container Types
item.description:
Spring’s container API has three distinct layers: bean metadata, the factory that creates objects from that metadata, and an application context that coordinates the factory with application services. Keeping those layers separate makes Spring source code and extension points easier to reason about.

Bean Definitions and Registries #

BeanDefinition is mutable metadata for one bean. It records the bean class or class name, scope, constructor arguments, property values, qualifiers, factory method, lifecycle methods, role, source location, and explicit dependencies. The parent/child metadata relationship is independent of Java inheritance.

item.title: Implementing Light and Dark Color Schemes
item.description:
A color-scheme implementation needs three layers:

  1. A system preference used when the visitor has made no site-specific choice.
  2. An explicit site preference that can override the system.
  3. Semantic colors that keep components independent from literal light and dark values.

Declare Semantic Colors #

Name variables by role rather than by appearance:

css 
:root {
 color-scheme: light dark;
 --surface: #ffffff;
 --surface-raised: #f5f6f8;
 --text: #17191c;
 --text-muted: #5d6470;
 --border: #d7dbe0;
 --accent: #1659b7;
}

body {
 color: var(--text);
 background: var(--surface);
}

color-scheme tells the user agent which schemes the page supports, allowing form controls, scrollbars, and system colors to match. It does not define the site’s custom palette.

item.title: Spring Conversion and Validation
item.description:
Spring treats conversion, presentation formatting, object binding, and validation as separate operations. A request parameter can therefore become a typed property and still produce structured errors without coupling the domain object to a web controller.

Conversion and Formatting #

ConversionService is the facade for type conversion. It can first answer whether a conversion is available and then convert by raw class or by TypeDescriptor, which preserves annotations and nested generic information.

item.title: C Library and glibc History
item.description: Linux applications depend on two different interfaces: the kernel system-call ABI and a C library. The ABI defines the transition into the kernel for a particular architecture. A C library implements the ISO C and POSIX interfaces that programs compile against, and it adds the process-startup code, dynamic loader, name-service lookup, threading support, locale handling, and many interfaces that do not map to one system call. The kernel therefore does not provide a complete C runtime.

item.title: Fixing CVEs for Golang-based statically-linked Executables
item.description:
gosu is a container-friendly alternative to su/sudo written in go. It’s included in the base image one of our production image, which triggers https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-68121.

Generic Considerations for all Golang-based statically-linked Executables #

CVEs in a statically-linked golang program come from 2 sources:

  1. The software’s own code. This is just good old software CVEs

Most times the Golang SDK is the one to blame, and fixing such CVEs is as simple as rebuild the program with latest golang SDK.

VS Code Virtual Space #

VS Code lacked virtual-space support for years. Issue microsoft/vscode#13960 tracked the feature from 2016 until it was finally resolved in 2024.

item.title: Spring MVC
item.description:
Spring MVC is the Servlet-based web framework in Spring Framework. Its front controller, DispatcherServlet, coordinates request mapping, argument resolution, controller invocation, return-value handling, and exception translation. Spring WebFlux uses a different reactive runtime and threading model; the two frameworks must not be treated as interchangeable.

Bootstrap and Dispatch #

A non-Boot Servlet application can register a web application context and dispatcher through WebApplicationInitializer:

java 
public final class WebInitializer implements WebApplicationInitializer {
 @Override
 public void onStartup(ServletContext servletContext) {
 var context = new AnnotationConfigWebApplicationContext();
 context.register(WebConfiguration.class);

 var servlet = servletContext.addServlet(
 "mvc", new DispatcherServlet(context));
 servlet.setLoadOnStartup(1);
 servlet.addMapping("/");
 }
}

Spring Boot performs equivalent registration for an MVC application. Mapping the dispatcher to / lets the Servlet container retain special handling for static resources and JSPs; /* also captures those dispatches.

item.title: QEMU
item.description:
QEMU provides system emulators, user-mode CPU emulators, and storage tools. A system emulator models a complete machine, including CPUs, memory, firmware, buses, and devices. A user-mode emulator translates a foreign-architecture userspace program and maps its system calls to the host kernel; it does not boot a guest kernel.

System Emulation #

qemu-system-x86_64 creates an x86-64 virtual machine. -m selects guest memory and -smp selects virtual CPUs. Firmware is part of the machine configuration: SeaBIOS provides legacy BIOS on x86, while OVMF provides UEFI firmware. Storage backends and devices are distinct: -blockdev defines a backend and -device attaches a guest controller or device. -drive is a convenient shorthand for common combinations.

item.title: Linux Process Model
item.description:
The kernel represents every schedulable flow of execution with struct task_struct, declared in the kernel source’s include/linux/sched.h. Distribution headers in /usr/include/linux are exported userspace ABI headers, not a copy of every kernel internal definition.

Tasks, Threads, and IDs #

A pid_t is an integer type; its width is architecture and ABI dependent. A struct pid represents an identity across PID namespaces and associates numeric PIDs with their namespaces. A task’s pid identifies that individual task in its active namespace. Its tgid is the thread-group ID: for the leader it equals pid, and getpid(2) returns the thread-group ID.

item.title: Color Theory and Color Spaces
item.description: Color theory becomes practical as soon as software has to map numbers to visible output. The underlying physics is simple, but the perceptual model is not.

item.title: Linux Administration Notes
item.description:
This collection covers several independent administration tasks: removable storage, capabilities, filesystem locations, image composition, and ELF symbol versions. Each section states the operational boundary that matters for automation.

Operating Removable Devices Safely #

Unmount every mounted filesystem before powering down removable media. udisksctl uses the UDisks service, so it applies desktop-session authorization and coordinates the operation instead of issuing an unmediated device command.

bash 
lsblk -o NAME,PATH,TYPE,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINTS
udisksctl unmount -b /dev/sdb1
udisksctl power-off -b /dev/sdb

Pass a partition such as /dev/sdb1 to unmount, but pass the whole drive such as /dev/sdb to power-off. The latter flushes buffers, removes the device from kernel use, and, when the hardware supports it, switches off the drive. Verify device names immediately before running the command because names can change across attachment events. A successful unmount alone does not guarantee that a USB enclosure has been powered off.

item.title: HTML Elements Reference
item.description: HTML elements are semantic building blocks, not just tags. Each element has content-model rules, permitted attributes, and browser behavior that can affect layout or accessibility.

item.title: DEFLATE and Gzip Formats
item.description:
DEFLATE is the bitstream format defined by RFC 1951. It combines an LZ77 sliding window with Huffman codes. “zlib” and “gzip” often refer to files that contain DEFLATE, but each is a different wrapper around the raw bitstream.

Block Boundaries and BTYPE #

A DEFLATE stream is a sequence of blocks. Each block begins at the current bit position with BFINAL (one bit) and BTYPE (two bits):

BTYPE Meaning
00 Stored bytes, without Huffman coding
01 Compressed with fixed Huffman codes
10 Compressed with dynamic Huffman codes
11 Reserved and invalid

BFINAL is one only for the last block. A compressed block ends when its literal/length stream emits end-of-block (EOB), symbol 256. The next block header follows immediately at the next bit; a compressed block is not padded to a byte boundary. Stored blocks are the exception: after their header, the decoder discards remaining bits in the current byte, reads little-endian LEN and NLEN (the one’s complement of LEN), and copies exactly LEN bytes. LEN is 16 bits, so one stored block holds at most 65,535 bytes.

item.title: C++ Language Rules and Named Requirements
item.description:
C++ language rules determine whether a program is well-formed and what its execution means. Library named requirements and concepts add contracts for generic code. Similar terminology can hide an important distinction: a compiler can check expressions and types, but it cannot prove every semantic, complexity, validity, or equality promise made by a type.

Definitions and the One-Definition Rule #

Every odr-used non-inline function or variable needs one definition in the program. Declarations can be repeated when compatible, which makes forward declarations possible.

item.title: Jenkins
item.description:
Jenkins coordinates delivery work as jobs and Pipelines. Store a Pipeline in a versioned Jenkinsfile because build logic, application code, and tool versions must change under the same review process.

Controller, Agents, and Workspaces #

The controller stores configuration and build records, evaluates scheduling decisions, serves the user interface, and coordinates agents. Builds should not run on the controller. An agent supplies one or more executors; each executor can occupy one Pipeline task at a time. Labels describe capabilities such as linux, arm64, or docker, and a Pipeline’s agent selection constrains where its workspace is allocated.

item.title: Xorg Display Server
item.description:
Xorg is an X11 display server. GUI programs use toolkits such as GTK or Qt and client libraries such as libX11 or libxcb to send X11 requests to it. The server manages input, outputs, and rendering; extensions such as GLX and XRender support accelerated rendering.

Connecting to a Display #

DISPLAY has the form [protocol/]host:display[.screen]. For the usual local display, :0 selects /tmp/.X11-unix/X0. TCP displays use port 6000 + display, though modern Xorg usually disables TCP listening. Once connected, the client and server exchange setup data, requests and replies, and asynchronous events such as key presses and expose notifications. SSH X11 forwarding creates a protected transport while retaining the protocol.

item.title: GnuPG Cheat Sheet
item.description:
The gpg command does a few distinct jobs:

  • manage OpenPGP keys, encrypt data to recipients
  • decrypt data for key holders, and
  • create or verify signatures.

Most common use case of GPG includes verifying an companion .asc file of a software release against its develoer’s public key, or signing your Git commits and tags with your secret key.

Installation #

sh 
# archlinux
# gnupg and pinentry should already be installed on your system as it is a dependency of pacman.

# debian/ubuntu
sudo apt install gnupg pinentry-curses pinentry-gtk-2

# redhat/fedora/centos
sudo dnf install gnupg2 pinentry # fedora/rhel 8+
sudo yum install gnupg2 pinentry # rhel 7

# mac
brew install gnupg pinentry-mac

GPG uses a program called pinentry to prompt for passphrases when unlocking private keys. The key design principle is separation: pinentry runs as a separate process, so the application requesting decryption never sees your passphrase - only the GPG agent does. This provides a trusted path between you and the crypto operations. Multiple variants exist: pinentry-curses (CLI), pinentry-gtk (GTK), pinentry-qt (Qt), pinentry-mac (macOS native), and others. You can configure which one to use in ~/.gnupg/gpg-agent.conf with the pinentry-program directive.

item.description: A trust store contains local trust anchors and, on some platforms, intermediate certificates or private-key entries. A verifier uses those anchors when it builds and validates an X.509 certification path. Installing a root therefore changes the security boundary of every client that reads that store.

item.title: Browser Content Disposition and Downloads
item.description:
Browsers decide whether to display a response, download it, or hand it to an external application from several inputs. Content-Disposition provides a strong preference, but content type, navigation context, sandboxing, browser capabilities, and user settings also affect the result.

Inline and Attachment Dispositions #

An attachment response requests a download:

http 
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/pdf
Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="guide.pdf"
Content-Length: 110352
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff

An inline response permits presentation inside the browser:

http 
Content-Type: application/pdf
Content-Disposition: inline; filename="guide.pdf"

inline does not guarantee display. The browser needs a viewer for the media type, and the user can configure some types to download instead. Omitting the header leaves the choice primarily to the media type and navigation context.

item.title: POSIX Time APIs
item.description:
Time APIs answer different questions: civil time names an instant, monotonic time measures an interval, and CPU clocks measure execution consumed by work. Selecting the wrong clock makes timeouts react to wall-clock corrections or makes I/O waits disappear from measurements.

Clock Selection #

clock_gettime reads a clockid_t into struct timespec, whose tv_sec and tv_nsec fields represent seconds and nanoseconds. POSIX requires CLOCK_REALTIME, the system civil clock measured from the Epoch, and CLOCK_MONOTONIC, whose origin is unspecified and cannot be set. Use realtime for timestamps and monotonic time for elapsed durations and deadlines.

item.title: The npm Ecosystem
item.description:
npm is the package manager distributed with Node.js. It installs packages, runs project scripts, publishes packages to registries, and records dependency resolutions so a team can reproduce an application build.

Package Metadata #

Every npm project is described by package.json. Its most important fields identify the package, define scripts, and declare dependencies:

json 
{
 "name": "example-service",
 "private": true,
 "type": "module",
 "scripts": {
 "test": "node --test",
 "start": "node src/server.js"
 },
 "dependencies": {
 "fastify": "^5.0.0"
 },
 "devDependencies": {
 "typescript": "^5.0.0"
 },
 "engines": {
 "node": ">=20"
 }
}

dependencies are needed in production. devDependencies support development, testing, or builds. A package marked private: true cannot accidentally be published.

item.title: Prometheus and PromQL
item.description:
• Prometheus for metrics
  • Loki or Elasticsearch for logs • Tempo or Jaeger for traces • Grafana as a unified interface

Prometheus is a monitoring system built around time-series data. It periodically scrapes metrics from applications, stores the samples locally, and provides PromQL (Prometheus Query Language) for querying them. Grafana can use Prometheus as a data source and turn the same queries into dashboards.

This article explains the Prometheus data model and the PromQL patterns needed for day-to-day monitoring.

item.description:
OpenSSL provides cryptographic primitives, protocol libraries, and command-line tools. Commands are useful for inspection, interoperability tests, and local administration; application code should use a maintained language library and its safe defaults.

Keys, CSRs, and Certificates #

Generate a private key with the generic key interface:

item.description:
Linux virtual memory gives each process a protected virtual address space while letting the kernel share files, overcommit address space, reclaim physical pages, and place memory on NUMA nodes. The discussion assumes a memory-management unit (MMU); Linux has a separate nommu implementation for systems without one.

Translation and TLBs #

item.title: Kotlin for Java Programmers
item.description:
Kotlin compiles to JVM bytecode and interoperates directly with Java, while adding null safety, concise declarations, extension functions, and structured concurrency.

Classes and Constructors #

A class has one primary constructor in its header and may have secondary constructors in its body. Primary-constructor parameters become properties only when marked val or var; initialization code belongs in an init block.

kotlin 
class Account(val id: String, initialBalance: Int) {
 var balance = initialBalance
 private set

 init {
 require(initialBalance >= 0)
 }

 constructor(id: String) : this(id, 0)
}

Secondary constructors must delegate to the primary constructor, directly or through another secondary constructor. Prefer the primary constructor plus default parameters when that expresses the API clearly.

item.title: Name Service Switch
item.description:
The GNU C Library’s Name Service Switch (NSS) separates an application’s lookup API from the data source that answers it. Code calls getpwnam(3), getgrnam(3), getaddrinfo(3), or getservbyname(3); glibc selects and combines services according to /etc/nsswitch.conf. Consequently, a local file, DNS server, directory service, or system service can provide the same category of information without changing callers.

Database Families #

glibc recognizes databases including passwd, group, shadow, hosts, networks, protocols, services, rpc, ethers, netgroup, aliases, publickey, and initgroups. Each has its own libc interfaces and record shape.

item.title: The C and C++ Preprocessor
item.description:
The preprocessor transforms preprocessing tokens before the C or C++ parser sees declarations, types, namespaces, or overloads. It expands includes, evaluates conditional directives, and performs macro replacement. Treat its output as generated source code, because language-level scope and type checking cannot repair an unsafe expansion.

Include Search Is a Build-Tool Contract #

#include "project/header.hpp" and #include <library/header> identify header-name tokens, not filesystem paths prescribed by the language standard. The mapping from a header name to a source file, including quote-versus-angle search order, is implementation-defined. Toolchains commonly search the including file’s directory and quote-specific paths for quotes, while angle headers begin in configured system paths; consult the compiler’s documentation and the build command for the actual order.

item.title: Spring Boot Actuator
item.description:
Spring Boot Actuator adds production-oriented monitoring and management features to a Spring Boot application. It exposes information such as health, metrics, configuration, log levels, and thread state through HTTP endpoints or JMX.

Actuator is part of the application itself. It is not a separate monitoring server and does not retain historical data. An endpoint reports the application’s current state; an external system such as Prometheus periodically collects that state and stores it over time.

item.title: Windows PE Format
item.description:
Portable Executable (PE) is the executable-image format used by Windows and by UEFI PE/COFF images. Unlike ELF, PE has no program-header table. The loader maps the image from the COFF header, optional header, section table, and data directories.

File Layout #

A PE image starts with a DOS header (MZ). Its e_lfanew member points to the NT headers, which begin with the PE\0\0 signature. A DOS stub follows the DOS header; some toolchains also emit a non-standard Rich header before the NT headers.

item.title: The CSS Box Model
item.description:
CSS lays out each element as one or more boxes. A basic box contains, from the inside outward, content, padding, border, and margin. Width calculations become predictable only after identifying which edge a declared size controls.

Content and Border Sizing #

The initial box-sizing value is content-box:

css 
.card {
 box-sizing: content-box;
 width: 20rem;
 padding: 1rem;
 border: 0.25rem solid;
}

The rendered border-box width is 22.5rem: 20 rem of content, 2 rem of horizontal padding, and 0.5 rem of border.

item.title: POSIX Threads
item.description:
POSIX threads provide concurrency in one process and one address space. Shared address space does not make shared mutable state safe: mutexes, condition variables, or C atomics must establish ownership and memory visibility.

Creation, Termination, and Cancellation #

pthread_create starts void *(*start_routine)(void *) with one pointer argument. It returns an error number directly, not through errno. A thread terminates by returning from its start routine, calling pthread_exit, or acting on cancellation; returning is equivalent to pthread_exit with that return value. Calling exit or returning from main terminates the entire process, whereas pthread_exit in the initial thread leaves other threads running.

item.title: Istio
item.description:
Istio applies traffic policy, identity, telemetry, and security policy to workloads through Envoy proxies and control-plane configuration. Adopt it only when those cross-cutting requirements justify the additional operational surface.

Data Plane and Control Plane #

The data plane consists of Envoy sidecars or an ambient deployment with a per-node ztunnel and optional waypoint proxies. istiod computes and distributes service discovery, certificates, and traffic configuration through xDS. A workload path captures inbound and outbound traffic according to the selected mode; traffic that bypasses that path cannot be governed by mesh policy. Ambient mode and sidecars have different L4/L7 enforcement placement, so migration must verify where each policy executes.

item.title: TLS 1.3
item.description:
This overview describes TLS 1.3. TLS carries a sequence of records. Before encryption, handshake data is carried in TLSPlaintext records; the legacy record-version field exists for interoperability and TLS 1.3 peers do not use it to negotiate the protocol. Records are limited to 2^14 bytes of content before permitted expansion.

Handshake #

The client sends ClientHello with a random value, supported cipher suites, key shares, extensions, and a legacy session ID. Its legacy_version is 0x0303; the supported-versions extension negotiates TLS 1.3. Current standard AEAD suites include AES-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305 with SHA-256 or SHA-384.

item.title: Responsive CSS and Layout
item.description:
Responsive layout should derive from content constraints instead of a list of device models. Intrinsic sizing, flexbox, grid, media queries, and container queries provide complementary controls.

Establish a Responsive Foundation #

The viewport declaration makes the CSS viewport match the device width:

html 
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">

Do not add user-scalable=no or a low maximum-scale; page zoom is an accessibility mechanism. Applications that position controls around an on-screen keyboard may also need the visual viewport API, because the visible area can change without the layout viewport changing.

item.title: Linux Seccomp
item.description:
Seccomp (secure computing) restricts the system calls a process may make. In strict mode, a process is limited to a small set of calls, historically read, write, _exit, and sigreturn on existing file descriptors. It is intentionally too narrow for most modern applications.

Filter mode attaches a classic BPF program that examines syscall numbers and selected arguments. The filter can allow, deny with an errno, kill the process, log, trace, or delegate a decision to a userspace notifier. Filters are monotonic: once installed, they cannot be relaxed. no_new_privs is normally required before an unprivileged process installs a filter, preventing the filter from being bypassed through a later privilege gain. Container runtimes use seccomp as one layer of defense, alongside namespaces, capabilities, and mandatory-access-control policy.

item.title: Disabling IPv6
item.description:
Disabling IPv6 removes IPv6-only reachability and can break loopback, container, DNS, and application assumptions. Diagnose address selection and connectivity before treating it as the remedy for a timeout.

Diagnose Address Selection First #

Name resolution can return both IPv6 and IPv4 addresses. A dual-stack client uses address-selection and connection-fallback logic; a failure can instead indicate DNS, a route, firewall policy, path MTU discovery, or a service bound only to IPv4.

item.title: util-linux
item.description:
util-linux is a collection of system utilities maintained as an independent upstream project. It supplies interfaces for block devices, mounts, terminals, sessions, namespaces, resource control, and data formatting. Distributions can split utilities into separate packages, so installed commands depend on packaging policy.

Operational Boundaries #

Commands that modify partitions, mounts, swap, device state, process credentials, or namespaces require suitable privileges. Inspect state before changing it, identify devices through stable attributes such as UUID or /dev/disk/by-id, and confirm a target is not mounted or in active use.

item.title: On Docker Image CVE Fixes and Prevention
item.description:
Rules of thumb:

  1. ensure your image have a proper security software-upgrade source configured - so apt-get upgrade (or the equivalent) doesn’t do nothing.
  2. Include RUN apt-get update && apt-get upgrade -y (or the equivalent) in your Dockerfile.
  3. In rare case involving statically-linked golang-based program, delete it or rebuild from source as part of your docker build.
  4. Schedule your own rebuild weekly or monthly.

Background #

  1. The single source of truth for Docker official images (DOI) is the master branch of https://github.com/docker-library/official-images. They use a format called “Library definition files” to define which tags in which repository should be actively rebuilt and where to find their Dockerfile (git repository URL and commit ID). These repo:tags are called currently maintained ones.
    • Most but not all of these referenced Dockerfile git repositories are maintained by Docker Inc. itself. For an example.
  2. A Jenkins job at https://doi-janky.infosiftr.net/ analyzes Dockerfiles of all DOIs, generates up-to-date dependencies among DOIs, and persists them to https://github.com/docker-library/meta.
  3. Using these metadata, every merged PR to a DOI Dockerfile triggers a rebuild and push to Docker Hub of all its downstream DOIs (those that FROM it) on https://doi-janky.infosiftr.net/.
    • Scheduled unconditional rebuilds are not guaranteed.

Observations #

  1. Docker Inc.’s DOIs do not RUN apt upgrade (or the equivalent) in the Dockerfile, nor are other DOI vendors required to do this.
  2. Even if a DOI vendor has the OS upgrade step in their Dockerfile, if there is no scheduled unconditional rebuild, security patches (if any) will not be installed.
  3. Some DOIs use a distro where security update upstream is disabled by default. See docker run --rm mysql:9.6.0 tail /etc/yum.repos.d/oracle-linux-ol9.repo for an example.

Consequently, currently maintained DOIs provide no guarantee of being CVE-free at the time of the build. Therefore, a no-op rebuild (without RUN apt upgrade or the equivalent) will not fix anything.

item.title: Java Class Loading
item.description:
Class loading converts a binary representation into a Class object. Linking and initialization are separate steps, thus loading a type does not imply that its static initializer has run.

Loaders and Type Identity #

The JDK supplies bootstrap, platform, and application loaders. The bootstrap loader defines core platform classes and is represented by null in selected APIs; the platform loader defines platform modules; the application loader loads application classes from the class path or module path. item.title: Linux Kernel Data Structures
item.description:
Linux’s list APIs are intrusive: linkage is embedded in the object owned by a subsystem. Intrusion removes a separate node allocation and lets one object participate in several indexes, but the container API does not own memory or provide synchronization.

Circular Doubly Linked Lists #

struct list_head contains only links:

c 
struct list_head {
 struct list_head *next, *prev;
};

struct job {
 unsigned long id;
 struct list_head pending_link;
 struct list_head owner_link;
};

A list head has the same type as an embedded node. In an empty list, next and prev both point back to the head. In a nonempty list, following either direction eventually returns to the head. Because the head is a sentinel rather than a payload object, iteration has no null terminator.

item.title: Linux GUI Applications in Containers
item.description:
Containers do not automatically have access to the host display session. A GUI client needs the appropriate display socket, environment variables, and credentials; exposing them grants the container meaningful control over the user session and should be done only for trusted images.

X11 #

For X11, mount the host socket directory—typically /tmp/.X11-unix—and pass DISPLAY. The client also needs the matching Xauthority cookie, usually supplied by mounting a narrowly scoped cookie file and setting XAUTHORITY. Do not use xhost +; it disables access control for the display. X11Docker can create a more constrained wrapper around this setup.

item.title: C++ Design Guidelines
item.description:
C++ interfaces should encode ownership, lifetime, and substitutability in types and signatures. The C++ Core Guidelines’ Rule of Zero follows from this design: a domain value composed from RAII members should not manually reproduce their copying, moving, and destruction behavior.

Resource Owners and Domain Values #

A resource-owning type acquires one resource, releases it in its destructor, and states whether copying or transfer is permitted. A handle represents access to a resource; an owning handle also bears responsibility for release. It is appropriate when a standard owner does not represent the resource’s acquisition, release, or error policy:

item.title: RISC-V Architecture Introduction
item.description:
RISC-V is an open instruction set architecture organized as a base integer ISA plus separately versioned extensions. The ISA defines instruction behavior and privileged execution; a platform profile, ABI, and execution environment add the requirements needed to run interoperable software.

Base Integer ISA and Register Convention #

RV32I and RV64I provide 32-bit and 64-bit integer registers respectively. Both define thirty-two general-purpose registers, x0 through x31. x0 always reads as zero and discards writes. The program counter is architecturally visible through control-flow effects rather than as a general-purpose register.

item.title: Linux Audio Architecture
item.description: Linux audio is a stack rather than one interchangeable API. ALSA exposes kernel sound devices and a user-space library. PulseAudio or PipeWire can then share those devices among applications, convert formats, mix streams, and apply desktop routing policy. Troubleshooting becomes deterministic when each layer is tested in signal-flow order.

item.title: VNC Ecosystem
item.description:
VNC transports a remote framebuffer and input events using the Remote Framebuffer protocol. It is useful for isolated graphical desktops, browser-delivered sessions, and container workloads that should not receive the host’s display socket.

Servers and Virtual Displays #

Xvfb is an in-memory X server with no physical display. x11vnc shares an existing X display through VNC; it does not itself create a virtual desktop. Other VNC servers, such as TigerVNC’s Xvnc, combine an X server with a VNC endpoint. noVNC is a WebSocket-to-VNC client that lets a browser connect through a compatible proxy.

item.title: Flex
item.description:
Flex generates a scanner from rules that map input text to C or C++ actions. A scanner normally supplies tokens to a parser, but it can also transform text or validate a regular-language format. The Flex manual defines generated interfaces and option-specific behavior.

Specification Structure #

A .l file has three sections separated by %%: definitions, rules, and user code. Definitions hold C declarations, named regular expressions, and start conditions. Rules pair patterns with actions. The final section supplies helper functions and, when needed, a driver.

item.title: Spring Thread Pools
item.description:
Spring’s TaskExecutor abstracts task submission. The common ThreadPoolTaskExecutor is a managed JavaBean wrapper around ThreadPoolExecutor; its pool, queue, rejection, and lifecycle choices still determine system capacity.

Defining and Naming an Executor #

Name executors by workload so callers select the intended resource:

java 
@Bean("reportExecutor")
ThreadPoolTaskExecutor reportExecutor() {
 var executor = new ThreadPoolTaskExecutor();
 executor.setCorePoolSize(8);
 executor.setMaxPoolSize(24);
 executor.setQueueCapacity(100);
 executor.setKeepAliveSeconds(30);
 executor.setThreadNamePrefix("report-");
 executor.setRejectedExecutionHandler(
 new ThreadPoolExecutor.CallerRunsPolicy());
 return executor;
}

Spring initializes and shuts down a ThreadPoolTaskExecutor as a managed bean. Returning its concrete type preserves lifecycle configuration and monitoring methods. Separate executors isolate workloads with different latency, blocking, priority, or downstream-capacity requirements.

item.title: x86 Protected Mode and Privilege
item.description:
x86 protected mode combines descriptor-based segmentation, controlled control transfers, paging, and privileged instructions. Long mode reduces ordinary segmentation but retains descriptor tables, privilege levels, interrupt gates, and a task-state segment (TSS). Operating systems use those mechanisms to enter the kernel and isolate user execution, while page tables provide the primary memory-protection boundary on current x86-64 systems.

Table Registers #

The global descriptor table (GDT) contains code, data, and system descriptors shared by a logical processor. GDTR stores the GDT’s linear base and byte limit. GDT entry zero is conventionally a null descriptor, which makes a selector with index zero unusable for ordinary code or data access.

item.title: Nginx Administration and Internals
item.description:
Nginx is an event-driven HTTP, stream, and mail proxy and server. Treat the configuration, its process privileges, and upstream timeouts as production code: validate changes before reloading and retain a known-good configuration.

Event-Driven I/O #

Nginx is built around nonblocking event loops. A master process reads the configuration and starts workers; each worker then waits on epoll, kqueue, or the platform’s equivalent readiness backend. The worker keeps a connection record for each peer and advances each request only when the socket becomes ready.

item.title: DDR SDRAM and Memory Modules
item.description:
Synchronous dynamic RAM stores charge in cells selected through a hierarchy of channels, ranks, banks, rows, and columns. DDR SDRAM adds transfers on both edges of the data clock, but the name of a DDR generation denotes a complete electrical and command protocol. DDR3, DDR4, and DDR5 modules are therefore not interchangeable even when their capacities match.

From Cells to Memory Channels #

Each DRAM die divides its cell array into banks. A bank has many rows, and its sense amplifiers also serve as a row buffer. Opening a row copies its cells into that buffer; a later column selection chooses a subset for transfer. DDR4 divides banks into bank groups because some command-to-command delays differ within and across groups.

item.title: Linux Keyboard Input
item.description:
Linux separates a keyboard’s transport-level report from a stable input key code and from the text or action produced by a keyboard layout. Keeping those layers distinct explains why a PS/2 and a USB keyboard can generate different hardware data but both report KEY_F.

Overview #

Input follows four conceptual stages:

  1. A transport driver receives bytes or reports. The atkbd driver handles AT and PS/2 scan-code sets, while usbhid parses USB HID usages.
  2. The driver parses make, break, prefix, and repeat state, then reports a Linux input key code such as KEY_F (33) with a press, release, or repeat value.
  3. The input core publishes events through evdev. A graphical compositor or input library normally applies its own layout to these events.
  4. For a Linux virtual console, the kernel keyboard layer applies the active console keymap and emits bytes, Unicode characters, strings, or console actions to the terminal layer.

A scan code is therefore not a character, and a Linux key code is not an X11, Wayland, or Unicode code point.

item.title: Spring Data JPA Specification API
item.description:
When a Spring Data JPA repository needs a WHERE clause that is optional, composable, and decided at runtime, the usual API is org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaSpecificationExecutor<T>.

It is the bridge between:

  1. Spring Data repository methods such as findAll(...), count(...), and exists(...)
  2. Spring’s org.springframework.data.jpa.domain.Specification<T>

item.title: Linux CPU Frequency Scaling
item.description:
Modern processors expose performance states that trade execution capacity against power and heat. Linux presents those controls through CPUFreq. “Frequency” remains in the interface for compatibility, although hardware-managed Intel HWP and AMD CPPC operate on performance requests rather than a discrete clock table.

CPUFreq’s Three Layers #

CPUFreq consists of:

  1. The core, which owns policy objects and the common sysfs interface.
  2. Governors, which convert workload demand into performance requests.
  3. Scaling drivers, which translate requests into platform-specific register, firmware, or hardware operations.

Only one struct cpufreq_driver can be registered at a time. The driver must therefore handle every CPU for which CPUFreq is available; heterogeneous systems still use policy objects to represent different control domains.

item.title: Testing C and C++ Programs
item.description:
C and C++ tests are executable programs whose status must affect the build and CI result. A framework can improve assertions and reporting, but a test executable with a dedicated main and deterministic dependencies is sufficient when integrated with the project’s test runner.

Build Tests as First-Class Targets #

Compile test targets separately from production binaries and link them against the production library. Register every executable with the existing test runner, such as CTest, Meson, or Automake TESTS, so a nonzero exit status fails CI.

item.title: Linux Control Groups Version 2
item.description:
Control groups (cgroups) account for and control sets of Linux tasks. A cgroup is not a process-tree node: a task inherits its parent’s cgroup when it forks, but a manager can subsequently migrate it. Consequently, cgroups provide the resource boundary behind service managers and containers, while namespaces provide views of global resources.

This article describes cgroup version 2 (cgroup v2). Its documented interface is the cgroup2 filesystem; files and supported controllers depend on the running kernel configuration and available hardware.

item.title: Maintaining AUR Packages
item.description:
The Arch User Repository stores Git repositories containing package recipes, not built packages. Maintaining an AUR package therefore means publishing a reviewable PKGBUILD and matching .SRCINFO, then validating that recipe in an isolated build environment.

Model the Package Correctly #

A PKGBUILD defines metadata such as pkgname, pkgver, pkgrel, arch, license, sources, checksums, and dependency arrays. Its functions separate stages:

  • prepare() applies patches or prepares sources.
  • build() compiles or generates software.
  • check() runs tests and requires checkdepends.
  • package() installs only below $pkgdir.

Use $srcdir for sources and build state; never write into the host filesystem from a package function. State runtime dependencies in depends, build-only tools in makedepends, and test-only packages in checkdepends. Missing declarations can remain hidden on a developer workstation and fail for users.

item.title: Docker-in-Docker
item.description:
Docker-in-Docker (DinD) runs a Docker daemon inside a container. It is sometimes useful for disposable CI jobs that must build or test images, but it adds privileged-kernel access, nested storage, and caching complexity. It is not the default choice for every job that invokes docker.

Choose the Right Build Model #

There are three common models:

  1. DinD: a dedicated daemon runs in the job network namespace. It provides separation from the host daemon but commonly needs privileged mode.
  2. Docker-outside-of-Docker: the job mounts the host Docker socket. It is simple and fast, but any process that can use the socket can control the host Docker daemon.
  3. Daemonless builders: BuildKit, Kaniko, Buildah, or a managed builder create OCI images without exposing a general-purpose host daemon.

Use the least privileged option that supports the build. Rootless BuildKit or a remote BuildKit builder can preserve cache efficiency without granting a CI job access to the runner’s Docker socket.

item.title: Variadic Programming in C and C++
item.description:
C++ variadic templates preserve the type and count of every argument. C ellipsis functions erase that information, which shifts type interpretation and argument-count discipline to the caller. Prefer C++ packs for new typed interfaces.

Packs, Expansions, and Folds #

A template parameter pack and a function parameter pack may contain zero or more elements. A pack expansion applies a pattern once per element.

cpp 
#include <utility>

template <class Function, class... Ts>
decltype(auto) invoke(Function&& function, Ts&&... values) {
 return std::forward<Function>(function)(std::forward<Ts>(values)...);
}

template <class... Ts>
auto sum(Ts... values) {
 return (0 + ... + values); // binary left fold; 0 is the empty-pack identity
}

std::forward preserves the value category deduced for each forwarding reference. It does not extend an argument’s lifetime, so a callee must still obey its ordinary reference and ownership contract.

item.title: Java Design Patterns
item.description:
Patterns name recurring design trade-offs. Java language features can implement a pattern, but neither a lambda nor a dependency-injection container is itself a replacement for a design decision.

Creational Patterns #

A Factory centralizes construction when callers must not depend on a concrete type or construction selects an implementation. A factory hides useful details, but a factory with a method for every product can become an unnecessary indirection.

java 
interface Parser { Document parse(String text); }
final class Parsers {
 static Parser forFormat(Format format) { return format::parse; }
}

A Builder collects optional arguments and validates cross-field invariants before producing an immutable value. Use a constructor or static factory when there are few mandatory fields; a builder that only mirrors setters obscures the required state. A Prototype is often clearer in Java as an explicit copy constructor or copyOf factory than Cloneable, whose shallow-copy and inheritance semantics are difficult to extend safely.

item.title: Browser Platform, Graphics, and Playwright in Docker
item.description:
Browser automation succeeds when tests model document loading, layout, networking, and rendering rather than treating a page as a static string.

Measure the Browser and DOM #

Browser dimensions answer different questions:

API Measurement

window.outerWidth and outerHeight Browser window bounds
