item.title: MySQL InnoDB Internals
item.description:
InnoDB stores table data and indexes in pages organized into tablespaces. A tablespace has a fixed page size, selected when the data directory is initialized. The default page size is 16 KiB. Page-oriented I/O explains why index locality, buffer-pool capacity, and row width affect query cost.

Data Dictionary and Metadata #

MySQL 8 stores the transactional data dictionary in InnoDB. Server metadata, including schemas, tables, columns, indexes, stored programs, and privileges, is therefore crash-safe and participates in atomic data-definition operations. Applications must use INFORMATION_SCHEMA, the Performance Schema, or SHOW statements to inspect metadata; internal dictionary tables are not an application interface.

item.title: Android Command-Line Tools
item.description:
Install the Android SDK command-line tools, platform tools, and the required platform or system image before using these commands. Set ANDROID_HOME to the SDK directory and add its cmdline-tools/latest/bin, platform-tools, and emulator directories to PATH.

Android Debug Bridge #

adb connects the host client to the local ADB server and the device-side adbd daemon. Select a target explicitly with -s SERIAL whenever more than one device or emulator is available.

item.title: Load Balancing
item.description:
Load balancing maps demand to healthy capacity while preserving transport and application semantics. Placement, health, retry, and overload policy form one system: an algorithm cannot recover capacity that health checks misclassify or retries consume.

Placement Layers #

  • DNS placement returns regional or service addresses. Resolver and client caching makes changes coarse-grained, so DNS cannot drain individual connections or react to per-request load.
  • Anycast placement advertises the same address from several sites and lets routing select a path. Route changes can move flows, and the nearest network path is not necessarily the site with spare application capacity.
  • Transport load balancing selects a backend from TCP, UDP, or QUIC flow metadata without interpreting the application request. Direct server return and connection tracking affect topology and failure behavior.
  • Reverse proxies terminate an application protocol and can route HTTP by authority, path, headers, method, or cookies. Termination enables retries and observability but consumes proxy capacity and creates another failure domain.
  • Application placement assigns work using domain state, such as tenant, shard ownership, queue partition, or accelerator availability. The application must then handle ownership changes and stale routing metadata.

Large systems combine layers: DNS or anycast chooses a site, an L4 load balancer chooses a proxy, and the proxy chooses a workload.

item.title: Browser Authentication
item.description:
Browser authentication assigns an application request to a user or workload identity. The application must define where credentials reside, which requests carry them, how the browser restricts them, and how the server invalidates them.

Sessions and Cookies #

For a browser application with a same-site backend, an opaque session identifier in a cookie keeps the credential out of JavaScript. Store session state server-side, rotate the identifier after authentication and privilege changes, and expire it on logout and inactivity.

Kconfig describes the choices from which a Linux kernel configuration is built. Kernel developers edit Kconfig files to define symbols and their relationships; users select values through front ends such as make menuconfig, make nconfig, make xconfig, or noninteractive targets such as olddefconfig.

The resulting .config is an input to Kbuild, not a complete build script. Configuration synchronization generates files consumed by Make and C, including include/config/auto.conf and include/generated/autoconf.h.

item.title: Kubernetes Access Control
item.description:
Kubernetes processes an API request through authentication, authorization, and admission control. Authentication establishes an identity; authorization determines whether that identity may perform an action; admission can validate or mutate the accepted object. These are separate controls and should be configured and audited separately.

Authenticate with OIDC #

OpenID Connect (OIDC) lets the API server validate bearer tokens issued by an external identity provider. The API server is configured with the issuer URL, client ID, and optional username and group claim mappings. The issuer must be reachable by the API server and its TLS certificate must validate.

item.title: C++ Initialization
item.description: Initialization gives an entity its first value or establishes a reference binding. Assignment changes an object that already exists. Because constructors participate only in initialization and assignment operators participate only after lifetime has begun, the distinction affects overload resolution, invariants, and performance.

item.title: MySQL Indexes
item.description:
InnoDB implements primary and secondary indexes with B+ trees. An index reduces I/O when its order matches selective predicates, joins, range scans, or ordering requirements; it increases write work and storage for every indexed row.

Clustered and Secondary Indexes #

An InnoDB table stores row data in its clustered index. InnoDB selects the declared primary key; otherwise it selects the first suitable non-null unique key, or creates an internal hidden key. Declare a short, stable primary key because each secondary-index entry stores the primary-key value.

item.title: Building and Starting Xorg
item.description:
The X.Org projects are hosted at https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/. The xorg/xserver project builds the X server executables, including X and Xorg. The xorg/app/xinit project builds xinit and its startx wrapper.

Starting a Session #

startx invokes xinit, which starts an X server and then a client session. With no explicit client script, it uses the conventional user configuration or system defaults. The server normally creates a local Unix socket such as /tmp/.X11-unix/X0 and sets a corresponding display number. Desktop display managers perform the same broad tasks but additionally manage login, seats, and session lifetime.

item.title: Kubernetes from Scratch
item.description:
Building Kubernetes from source is suitable for studying or testing a patched component. A production cluster also requires a supported upgrade path, certificate rotation, backup recovery, networking, storage, monitoring, and incident procedures.

Object Model and API Paths #

Kubernetes models cluster operations as CRUD on resources. Each object has a UID, a type, a unique name within that type, labels for indexed selection, and annotations for non-identifying metadata.

item.title: Linux Socket System
item.description:
A socket is a file descriptor representing one endpoint of a communications channel. Programs create one with socket(2), then usually bind or connect it and use read(2)/write(2) or send(2)/recv(2).

c 
int sockfd = socket(int domain, int type, int protocol);

The domain selects an address family such as AF_INET, AF_INET6, AF_UNIX, or AF_NETLINK. The type selects a semantic such as SOCK_STREAM, SOCK_DGRAM, or SOCK_SEQPACKET; the protocol normally selects a concrete protocol within that combination, or 0 selects the default.

item.title: Server-Driven HTTP Traffic
item.description:
Server-driven HTTP lets a server send information without a new client request for every update. Server-Sent Events (SSE) is a simple standardized option for one-way server-to-browser updates.

Server-Sent Events #

An SSE client makes a normal GET request with an Accept: text/event-stream header. The server replies with 200 OK, Content-Type: text/event-stream, and keeps the response open while sending UTF-8 event fields separated by a blank line:

text 
event: order-updated
id: 42
data: {"status":"paid"}

In browsers, EventSource reconnects automatically. The server can send retry: to suggest a reconnection delay, and the browser sends Last-Event-ID after a reconnect when an event ID was received. Design the stream so clients can resume from that ID or refresh a snapshot safely.

item.title: Go Language and Templates

Go organizes source into packages and modules, reports recoverable failures as values, and provides reflection-based text and HTML templates in its standard library. The same design principle connects these areas: make dependencies and control flow explicit at the API boundary.

Modules, Packages, and Builds #

A package is the compilation and namespace boundary formed by non-test .go files with the same package declaration in one directory. A module is a versioned collection of packages rooted at go.mod. The module path supplies the import-path prefix:

item.title: x86 and x86-64 Instruction Encoding
item.description:
x86 uses variable-length instructions. An instruction can contain legacy prefixes, an opcode, a ModR/M byte, a scale-index-base (SIB) byte, a displacement, and an immediate. Only the opcode is always present:

Long mode can add a REX prefix between the legacy prefixes and opcode. VEX, XOP, and EVEX encodings replace parts of this layout for newer instruction families. Regardless of the form, an architectural x86 instruction cannot exceed 15 bytes.

item.title: UEFI and EDK II
item.description:
UEFI is the firmware interface between platform firmware and an operating system. The UEFI Forum publishes the UEFI and Platform Initialization (PI) specifications; EDK II is the TianoCore reference implementation and build environment.

Boot Phases #

The PI architecture divides early firmware execution into phases. Pre-EFI Initialization (PEI) begins with little more than the CPU and temporary storage. The PEI Foundation runs PEI modules (PEIMs), publishes PPIs (PEIM-to-PEIM interfaces), and uses hand-off blocks (HOBs) to describe discovered resources. Its central job is to initialize sufficient RAM for the next phase.

item.title: Building AOSP
item.description:
An Android Open Source Project checkout and its build artifacts require substantial disk space; the exact requirement depends on the branch, target, and enabled variants. Use a 64-bit Linux host with ample RAM, fast storage, and enough free space for both the checkout and the output directory.

Obtaining the Source #

AOSP is distributed across many Git repositories. The repo tool coordinates those repositories from a manifest; it is a Python wrapper around Git rather than a source control system of its own. Initialize the required branch with repo init, then use repo sync to populate or update the checkout.

item.title: Helm and Argo CD
item.description:
Helm renders versioned Kubernetes manifests from a chart, values, and templates. Helm records release metadata in the cluster, while Kubernetes reconciles only the resulting resources; Kubernetes does not understand or maintain Helm templates.

Helm Releases #

Keep default values in values.yaml, use environment-specific values files or explicit --set values sparingly, and validate rendered output before applying it:

sh 
helm lint charts/orders
helm template orders charts/orders -f values-production.yaml
helm upgrade --install orders charts/orders -f values-production.yaml --namespace orders --create-namespace --atomic

--atomic rolls back a failed upgrade when Helm can determine failure, but it does not make externally managed state transactional. Define hooks, CRDs, database migrations, and rollback behavior explicitly.

item.title: Compiler Builtins and Bit Operations
item.description:
GCC and Clang provide builtin spellings for operations that their front ends recognize directly. Bit-counting builtins can lower to a target instruction, a library sequence, or an optimized expression depending on the selected target and optimization context. Source code should choose the interface that states its portability and zero-input contract.

item.title: x86 Instruction Families
item.description:
x86 groups a large, irregular instruction set behind common data movement, arithmetic, bit manipulation, control-flow, and string-processing patterns. Operand size, address size, execution mode, prefixes, and ISA extensions can change an instruction’s encoding or availability. Intel’s and AMD’s architecture manuals remain authoritative; successful assembly only proves that a tool can encode the source.

Data Movement and Address Generation #

MOV copies an immediate or register value to a register or memory, or copies memory to a register. An ordinary MOV has at most one explicit memory operand. MOVZX zero-extends a narrower integer, while MOVSX and MOVSXD sign-extend. A 32-bit general-purpose-register destination in 64-bit mode implicitly clears the upper 32 bits.

item.title: TCP
item.description:
TCP is a reliable, ordered byte-stream transport. It identifies each byte with a 32-bit sequence number; arithmetic on those numbers is modulo 2^32.

Three-Way Handshake #

To open a connection, the client sends a SYN with an initial sequence number x. The server replies with SYN+ACK, chooses its own initial sequence number y, and acknowledges x + 1. The client sends an ACK acknowledging y + 1. A SYN consumes one sequence-number position even though it carries no application byte.

item.title: Querying HTML, Media, and Storage
item.description:
Web extraction, media processing, and storage formats all benefit from working with structured representations rather than treating bytes as opaque text.

Parse HTML Before Querying It #

XPath operates on a document tree, not a raw HTML string. Parse web content with an HTML parser, then query the resulting DOM. Browser DOMs, HTML parsers, and XML parsers can repair malformed markup differently, so use the same parser class in tests and production.

item.title: Docker Fundamentals
item.description:
Docker, the container system that still depends on your kernel, your CPU ISA, and its x86-64 syscall. An application that runs in a docker container is said to be containerized.

Component Overview #

Docker Engine: dockerd #

dockerd is a CLI daemon program that manages installed containers on the local system. It is branded as Docker Engine or Docker CE (Community Edition), and is open-source and free.

The dockerd daemon listens on the UNIX domain socket /var/run/docker.sock for incoming clients. This socket file must be readable by the user who runs a docker client to establish the socket (to send HTTP request). If you installed the Docker Engine from your Linux distro’s package manager, this socket file may be only readable by the root or a special user group dedicated to Docker, e.g. docker. You may choose to add yourself to that user group, or simply become root whenever using the docker client. Use docker info to check if the dockerd is running and the client has permissions.

item.title: Gradle
item.description:
Gradle is a build automation tool for JVM projects and many other ecosystems. Build logic is written in the Groovy DSL (.gradle) or Kotlin DSL (.gradle.kts). Gradle itself runs on the JVM.

Project Files #

From a repository root, the important files are:

  • settings.gradle[.kts] defines the build and includes subprojects. It is required for a multi-project build and may set the root project name.
  • build.gradle[.kts] defines plugins, dependencies, tasks, and conventions for the root project or a subproject.
  • gradle.properties holds project properties. User-wide properties may live in ~/.gradle/gradle.properties.
  • gradlew, gradlew.bat, and gradle/wrapper/ form the Gradle Wrapper and should be committed.
  • .gradle/ is local Gradle state and should be ignored.

Use include("service", "web") in settings.gradle.kts to register subprojects. Each subproject can have its own build script while sharing repository-wide conventions.

item.title: Android System Architecture
item.description:
Android uses the Linux kernel for scheduling, process isolation, device drivers, networking, and filesystems, but supplies its own native library, runtime, framework, and application model. Bionic is Android’s C library. ART executes DEX bytecode, and Binder provides the principal cross-process RPC mechanism.

Runtime and Process Creation #

Build tools compile Java or Kotlin sources to class files and then transform them into DEX code. An APK or app bundle delivery split packages DEX, resources, native libraries, signing metadata, and a manifest. ART compiles and interprets DEX as appropriate for the device and profile state; an APK is not simply an executable JAR.

item.title: GNU Info
item.description:
GNU Info is the terminal reader for manuals generated from Texinfo. It is not a pager for a linear text file: an Info file contains named nodes joined by menus, cross-references, and Next, Prev, and Up pointers. An installed manual can be split across several compressed filesystem files, but Info presents it as one manual.

Start with the Manual Tree #

Run info without an argument to open the directory node, the installed manual tree. Run info coreutils or info '(coreutils)Top' to open a named manual and node.

item.title: LR Parsing
item.description:
LR parsing is a table-driven bottom-up method for deterministic context-free grammars. L means tokens are read left to right; R means the parser constructs a rightmost derivation in reverse.

Shift-Reduce Machine #

The parser maintains a stack of states and grammar symbols. For each state and lookahead token, an action table chooses one of:

  1. Shift: consume the token and push the destination state.
  2. Reduce: replace the right-hand side of a production with its left-hand-side nonterminal, then use the goto table to select the next state.
  3. Accept: recognize the augmented start production at end of input.
  4. Error: report that no valid continuation exists.
text 
push state 0
repeat
 action = ACTION[top_state, lookahead]
 if action is shift s: consume lookahead; push s
 if action is reduce A → β: pop |β| grammar symbols and states; push GOTO[top_state, A]
 if action is accept: return syntax tree
 otherwise: report a syntax error

Semantic actions commonly run on reduction. A parallel value stack stores AST nodes or other values for the symbols being reduced.

item.title: Algorithm Analysis and Complexity Classes
item.description:
Algorithm analysis establishes how an algorithm’s resource requirements grow with its input. It supports design decisions before implementation details, hardware, and representative workloads obscure the dominant cost. A useful analysis identifies the input size, specifies the resource, and states the cost model before deriving a bound.

Defining the Cost #

Choose a size parameter that represents the input. An array algorithm often uses \(n\), whereas a graph algorithm needs both its vertices \(V\) and edges \(E\). State the resource as well: comparison count, memory consumption, disk I/O, network round trips, or elapsed time under a defined machine model.

item.title: PowerShell Splatting and Hashtable Values
item.description:
PowerShell splatting passes a hashtable or array as named or positional arguments. It avoids repeating long parameter lists and keeps configuration separate from a command invocation.

Splatting PowerShell Commands #

Prefix a hashtable variable with @ at the call site:

powershell 
$request = @{
 Uri = 'https://api.example.test/items'
 Method = 'Get'
 Headers = @{ Accept = 'application/json' }
 TimeoutSec = 30
}

Invoke-RestMethod @request

Hashtable keys must match parameter names, including supported aliases. Splatting does not expand arbitrary strings into shell syntax; PowerShell binds the resulting values as typed command arguments.

item.title: CDN Origin Routing
item.description:
CDN routing has two separate decisions: where a client connects and which origin the edge contacts. DNS and anycast choose an edge location; configuration at that edge chooses an origin and constructs the upstream request. Keeping those decisions separate makes failures easier to diagnose.

Request Identity at the Edge #

A client starts with a URL such as https://www.example.com/docs. DNS returns an edge address, TLS SNI identifies www.example.com during the handshake, and the HTTP request carries Host: www.example.com (or the equivalent :authority field in HTTP/2 and HTTP/3). The CDN uses this hostname and path to select a distribution and cache behavior.

item.title: Linux Namespaces
item.description:
Namespaces partition names and resource views that would otherwise be global. Each task has one namespace instance of each supported type, and tasks in the same instance observe the same instance-specific resources. Namespaces do not, by themselves, constrain CPU, memory, or I/O consumption; cgroups provide those resource controls.

Linux exposes eight namespace types. Time namespaces were added in Linux 5.6; the other types predate that release. The namespace flags in include/uapi/linux/sched.h are the version-specific source of truth.

item.title: Helm Operations and Argo CD Migrations
item.description:
Moving static Kubernetes manifests into Helm and then into Argo CD is a change in ownership as well as templating. Inventory the live resources, preserve immutable names and storage, and make the desired state reproducible before turning on automated pruning.

Understand Helm’s Release Model #

For a direct Helm release, an upgrade compares the previous release manifest, the newly rendered manifest, and the live object. Resources present in both manifests are updated when their fields permit it; resources only in the new manifest are created; resources removed from the chart are normally deleted. Immutable fields can require an explicit replacement strategy.

item.title: x86 and x86-64 Architecture Overview
item.description:
x86 began with Intel’s 16-bit 8086. The 80286 introduced protected mode, IA-32 established the 32-bit programming model and paging, and AMD64 extended the architecture to 64-bit execution. Intel calls the combined architecture Intel 64 and IA-32; AMD documentation uses AMD64. Vendor names do not determine every feature, so software must discover extensions explicitly.

Byte Order and Operand Sizes #

item.title: Java Concurrency and Executors
item.description:
Executor separates submitting a Runnable from deciding where it runs. ExecutorService adds lifecycle management and submit; Callable<V> can return a value or throw a checked exception, and Future<V> represents the eventual result. Future.get() establishes the required visibility of actions performed by the task before completion.

java 
Future<Result> future = pool.submit(() -> compute(input));
try {
 return future.get();
} catch (ExecutionException e) {
 throw new ServiceException(e.getCause());
}

Use synchronized, Lock, atomics, concurrent collections, or message passing to establish happens-before relationships. An executor supplies scheduling, not automatic safety for mutable shared objects.

item.title: JSON Canonicalization
item.description:
JSON canonicalization turns semantically equivalent JSON data into one deterministic byte sequence. It is useful before hashing, signing, comparing, or using JSON as an identity key. Ordinary JSON serialization is not enough: object-member order, whitespace, escaping, and number formatting can differ without changing the data model.

JSON Canonicalization Scheme #

RFC 8785 defines the JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS). It uses the ECMAScript JSON serialization rules, serializes object properties in lexicographic order of UTF-16 code units, emits no insignificant whitespace, and requires valid I-JSON input.

item.title: Linux File Descriptors
item.description:
Linux separates a process’s integer handle from the kernel object that stores an open instance’s state. The distinction explains offset sharing, duplication, inheritance, and many descriptor leaks.

Descriptor Tables and Open-File Descriptions #

A file descriptor is a nonnegative integer indexing the calling process’s descriptor table. A table entry references an open-file description, represented inside Linux by struct file. The open-file description records state such as:

  • the current file offset;
  • file status flags such as O_APPEND and O_NONBLOCK;
  • the opened path, access mode, credentials, and file operations.

Each successful open() normally creates a new open-file description and installs a reference in the process table. Opening the same path twice therefore creates independent offsets:

item.title: C++ Ranges and Views
item.description:
The ranges library separates the ability to iterate from ownership, traversal strength, and lazy transformation. A range supplies iteration boundaries; a view is a range suited to adaptor pipelines; an adaptor builds a new view whose elements are evaluated when iteration requests them.

cpp 
#include <ranges>
#include <vector>

std::vector<int> source{1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
auto even_squares = source
 | std::views::filter([](int value) { return value % 2 == 0; })
 | std::views::transform([](int value) { return value * value; });

Constructing even_squares does not transform every element. Iteration invokes the predicate and transformation, so changes to source before iteration can be observed subject to the source container’s invalidation rules.

item.title: MySQL Tables and Views
item.description:
A base table persists rows. A view persists a query definition and presents its result as a table-like object. SHOW FULL TABLES distinguishes them, and INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES.TABLE_TYPE reports BASE TABLE or VIEW.

InnoDB Row Formats #

InnoDB supports REDUNDANT, COMPACT, DYNAMIC, and COMPRESSED row formats. DYNAMIC is the current default. For variable-length columns, InnoDB can store long values on overflow pages and retain a reference in the clustered record. The precise inline and overflow behavior depends on the row format, page size, column type, and value length; schema design should avoid assuming that a TEXT or BLOB value occupies a fixed in-row size.

item.title: Electromagnetism

Classical electromagnetism describes electric and magnetic fields, their sources, their forces on matter, and their propagation. Circuit models approximate those fields when component dimensions are small compared with the relevant wavelengths. High-frequency interconnects require a field or transmission-line model because voltage and current no longer change everywhere at once.

item.title: Kubernetes Federation
item.description:
Kubernetes Federation was an early attempt to manage workloads across clusters from a federation control plane. Federation v1 was deprecated, and its CRD-based successor, commonly called KubeFed or Federation v2, is no longer an active Kubernetes project. It should be treated as historical technology rather than the basis for a new platform.

What Federation Tried to Solve #

The model registered member clusters and propagated selected resources to them. It aimed to centralize placement, replica distribution, service discovery, and configuration while retaining independent clusters. The hard parts were conflict handling, cluster failure, networking, identity, version skew, and the fact that a single global API could become another availability dependency.

item.title: Linux Kernel Release Lifecycle
item.description:
Linux development follows a time-based cycle around the mainline Git tree maintained by Linus Torvalds. Mainline development, stable backports, and distribution kernels are related but distinct release streams.

Mainline Development #

Most patches move through a hierarchy rather than going directly to Linus. A developer posts a patch to the relevant mailing list; reviewers and a subsystem maintainer evaluate it; the maintainer stages accepted work in a subsystem tree. Lower-level trees can feed higher-level trees, such as a driver tree feeding a networking tree. Integration in linux-next exposes conflicts between subsystem trees before they reach mainline. During the merge window, top-level maintainers send signed pull requests to Linus’s tree.

item.title: MongoDB Views
item.description:
MongoDB views are read-only query definitions over a collection or another view. A view stores its aggregation pipeline, not the pipeline result, so each read applies the pipeline to the current source data. A standard view therefore does not provide materialized-view caching.

db.createView() takes a target collection name, a source namespace, and an aggregation pipeline:

item.title: CPU Architecture Overview
item.description:
A processor implements an instruction set architecture (ISA): the contract that defines instructions, registers, data types, address formation, exceptions, and privilege behavior. A microarchitecture implements that contract with pipelines, execution units, caches, predictors, and internal queues. Programs observe architectural state; performance depends on microarchitectural state.

From Fetch to Retirement #

At a conceptual level, a processor fetches instruction bytes, decodes an instruction, obtains operands, executes the operation, accesses memory when required, and commits the result. A simple processor can perform those steps sequentially. A pipelined processor overlaps steps from several instructions, thus improving throughput without requiring every instruction to have low latency.

item.title: DNS Resolution Model
item.description:
DNS names form a rooted tree. A domain is the subtree rooted at a name. A zone is an administrative portion of that tree served as authoritative data. Domain and zone are therefore not synonyms: a zone can delegate a child subtree and no longer contain its authoritative records.

Delegation and Authority #

The parent zone delegates child.example. by publishing NS records at that name. The child zone publishes its own apex SOA and NS records. A resolver asking the parent for data below that cut receives a referral with the child’s NS RRset in the Authority section.

item.title: MySQL Variables and Prepared Statements
item.description:
MySQL distinguishes server system variables, local routine variables, and session user variables. Their scope and evaluation rules differ, so they should not be used interchangeably.

System and User Variables #

System variables use @@ and may have global, session, or both scopes:

sql 
SELECT @@GLOBAL.transaction_isolation, @@SESSION.sql_mode;
SET SESSION sql_safe_updates = 1;

Changing a global variable affects new sessions when the variable also has a session scope; it is not a way to change an existing connection’s transaction policy. A dynamic variable can change at runtime, whereas a read-only variable requires startup configuration. SET PERSIST changes the runtime global value and writes mysqld-auto.cnf; SET PERSIST_ONLY writes the persisted value without changing runtime state. Verify that a variable is persistable before using either form, and keep file ownership with the server rather than editing that generated file.

item.title: GCC Driver and Toolchain
item.description:
gcc and g++ are GCC driver programs. They select a language front end from input suffixes and options, run preprocessing and compilation, invoke the assembler, and coordinate the linker. The GCC manual is authoritative because exact defaults depend on the configured target and GCC release.

Driver Stages and Language Defaults #

Small library contracts frequently determine correctness more than API surface area. The following rules prevent common Java integration failures.

Object Contracts #

equals must be reflexive, symmetric, transitive, consistent, and false for null. If two objects are equal, they must have the same hashCode; therefore override both before using a value as a hash key. Do not mutate equality fields while an object is a map key. Prefer composition over inheritance when equality would otherwise break symmetry.

item.title: IMAP4rev2
item.description:

Connection and Commands #

IMAP uses a text protocol over TCP. Port 143 begins in cleartext and can negotiate TLS with STARTTLS; port 993 uses TLS from connection establishment. Clients must obtain capabilities, negotiate TLS before password authentication, and require certificate and hostname validation.

item.description:
A template is a declaration family parameterized by types, constant values, templates, and packs. A specialization is formed under C++ name lookup, type checking, overload resolution, and constraint rules; templates are not textual substitution.

Template Parameters #

Type parameters accept types, constant template parameters accept structural constant values, and template template parameters accept a compatible template. Defaults provide omitted arguments. A parameter pack represents zero or more parameters or arguments.

item.title: Clang-Format
item.description:
clang-format makes source layout a repository policy rather than a per-author preference. It formats supported languages from a syntactic token stream, so indentation, wrapping, and many spacing decisions are reproducible. It does not establish naming, API, ownership, or behavioral correctness; review must still examine those semantic concerns.

Establishing Repository Policy #

Commit a .clang-format file at the repository root. With --style=file, clang-format searches from each input file toward its ancestor directories and selects the closest .clang-format or _clang-format. A nested directory can therefore deliberately override a root policy, but an accidental nested file changes the result for that subtree.

item.title: Supervisord
item.description:
Supervisor is a process-control system for Unix-like hosts. It starts configured programs, captures their output, restarts them when appropriate, and exposes a control interface. It is useful when an application needs a lightweight, explicit process manager, but it is not a substitute for the operating system’s init system or service manager.

Define a Program #

A minimal program definition belongs in Supervisor’s included configuration directory:

ini 
[program:worker]
command=/opt/app/bin/worker --queue=default
directory=/opt/app
user=app
autostart=true
autorestart=unexpected
startsecs=5
stopasgroup=true
killasgroup=true
stdout_logfile=/var/log/app/worker.log
stderr_logfile=/var/log/app/worker-error.log

startsecs prevents a process that exits immediately from being reported as successfully started. stopasgroup and killasgroup help ensure that child processes receive termination signals during a restart. Run the service as an unprivileged user and grant only the filesystem access it needs.

item.title: glibc User Databases
item.description:
The user database maps login names and numeric user IDs to account records. /etc/passwd is the familiar representation, but an application must not assume that the file is the authoritative source. glibc resolves the passwd database through the Name Service Switch (NSS), whose passwd: entry in /etc/nsswitch.conf can consult local files, systemd, LDAP, NIS, or other installed providers.

PAM does not perform these lookups. PAM handles authentication and account-management policy, whereas NSS answers identity database queries.

item.title: pacman
item.description:
pacman manages installed package records and configured Arch repositories. The local database records installed versions, reasons, files, and ownership; sync databases describe repository packages. Keep those views coherent by refreshing and upgrading in one transaction.

Inspect the Local Database #

Use -Q for installed-package queries:

sh 
pacman -Qs '^bash$'
pacman -Qi bash
pacman -Ql bash
pacman -Qo /usr/bin/pacman
pacman -Qk

-Ql lists files supplied by an installed package, -Qo finds the owner of an existing path, and -Qk checks tracked files. pacman -F instead searches the repository file database; populate it first with sudo pacman -Fy.

item.title: C++ Value Categories and Move Semantics
item.description:
Move semantics are overload selection and type-defined state transfer, not an automatic transfer of ownership. Begin with an expression’s value category, then choose a parameter type that describes ownership and lifetime.

Expression Categories #

Every non-void expression is exactly one of these categories:

  • An lvalue identifies an object, function, or bit-field.
  • An xvalue identifies an object whose resources may be reused.
  • A prvalue computes a value or initializes an object.

Lvalues and xvalues are glvalues; prvalues and xvalues are rvalues. A named variable is an lvalue expression even when it has type T&&.

An annotation is metadata attached to a declaration or type use. It is not a general-purpose object literal: an annotation type is a special interface whose members describe the permitted metadata.

Annotation members have no parameters or type parameters, and may not declare a throws clause. item.title: Misc Algorithms
item.description:
Use standard-library algorithms when their contract fits the task because their implementations optimize for the target platform.

Nearest Smaller Element to the Left #

Maintain increasing values on the stack. Each index is pushed and popped once, giving \(O(n)\) time and \(O(n)\) space.

cpp 
#include <cstddef>
#include <vector>

std::vector<int> nearest_left_smaller(const std::vector<int>& values) {
 std::vector<int> result(values.size(), -1);
 std::vector<std::size_t> stack;
 stack.reserve(values.size());

 for (std::size_t index = 0; index < values.size(); ++index) {
 while (!stack.empty() && values[stack.back()] >= values[index]) {
 stack.pop_back();
 }
 if (!stack.empty()) {
 result[index] = static_cast<int>(stack.back());
 }
 stack.push_back(index);
 }
 return result;
}

Use > instead of >= when an equal predecessor is valid. Reversing the scan or comparison produces next-greater, stock-span, histogram, and temperature-query variants.
